authorization_condition: RBC-009 is COMPLETE: SPARE-F004 is proven to DOMAIN_TESTED against CI run 33314202480, green on all three jobs. RBC-010 (broad fan-out) is the remaining bootstrap task and is now unblocked. Two cautions before authorising it: source-map reports 21 unclaimed source files, and CT-7 stands at 23 of 206 acceptance contracts, so fan-out would largely build against the generic contracts CT-1 exists to prevent. No independent specialist review has been performed on the pilot.
status_change_note: v2.1 reported CT-1 and CT-2 GREEN on a distinctness metric computed over command and event NAMES. Those names embed their own aggregate name, so they are distinct by construction. Re-scored on semantics (CT-7), both drop to AMBER. This is a correction to the measurement, not a regression in the work: no contract was removed or weakened. As of 2026-08-30 the module-expansion packages were adopted: 186 -> 206 features. Breadth increased; contract depth did not, so CT-1/CT-2/CT-7 remain AMBER by design rather than by oversight.

closure_tests.why_amber: CT-1 requires a per-feature acceptance contract and per-feature permissions. One acceptance contract and two permission skeletons cover all 186 features, and 67 features share a single Create/Start/Block/Resume/Complete/Cancel skeleton. The structural elements are present; the feature-specific content is not yet.
closure_tests.remedy: Author per-feature acceptance contracts and permission sets ahead of each feature entering implementation, starting with the pilot's bounded context. Tracked by CT-7 against a committed baseline.

closure_tests.why_amber: CT-2 requires tests per eventuality contract. Eight test definitions span 254 contracts, and two of those eight are themselves generic. Every material contract does carry owner queue, commands, procedure, evidence and terminal states, so the structure holds — the executable part does not yet.
closure_tests.remedy: Write real test definitions for material, customer-visible, money- and safety-touching contracts first. The bespoke examples already in the registry (damage before POD, offline-before-submit, timeout-then-success) are the pattern to follow.

closure_tests.why_it_exists: CT-1 and CT-2 were reported green by counting interpolated names. CT-7 measures the property those tests were meant to assert, and blocks regression so the registries can only become more specific.

pack_lineage_note: v2.1 was authored as a 12-file overlay on v2.0 but packaged as a replacement pack, dropping 181 files including 33 machine registries and the ready-to-apply repository bootstrap. v2.2 restores the v2.0 substrate underneath the v2.1 decisions. agent:manifest-check now fails when a manifest is incomplete or a canon-referenced path is absent, so an overlay cannot again be mistaken for a replacement.
